text: A neutral daily trainer with a traditional, fairly high heel-to-toe drop and balanced cushioning that feels neither very soft nor firm.
Medium-volume upper with a padded heel collar that holds the heel securely; the toe box is moderate, not especially roomy.
Offered in wide and extra-wide versions, a common pick for runners with a wide forefoot who want a familiar, conventional fit.
A stability shoe with guide rails at the heel that keep the foot centered; the guidance is mild rather than rigid.
Fit is close to the Ghost: medium volume, secure heel, moderate toe box, with a slightly more structured midfoot.
Available in wide and extra-wide widths, so it suits wide feet that want a stable, conventional ride.
Brooks' most cushioned neutral trainer, with a soft, plush ride aimed at easy and long runs.
A plush, padded upper with a fairly high-volume feel; runners with a low instep may need to lace it tighter to lock the midfoot.
Heel counter and collar give a secure, cushioned heel hold.
A bouncy, energetic daily trainer with a high stack of soft foam; feels lively rather than mushy.
The toe box is generally described as comfortable with room to splay; the upper is light and fairly low volume.
Heel hold is adequate but not the most locked-in; a runner-loop lacing helps with heel slip.
A max-cushion neutral trainer with a soft, protective ride for long easy miles.
A knit upper with a padded, high-volume feel and a roomy forefoot; secure heel with a thick collar.
Comes in wide and extra-wide versions, suiting wide feet that want a lot of cushioning.
A cushioned stability trainer; the stability is built into a wider base and firmer medial side rather than a hard post.
Medium to high upper volume with a secure, structured heel counter; the toe box is moderate.
Offered in wide and extra-wide versions.
A lightweight, well-cushioned daily trainer with a rocker shape that rolls the foot forward smoothly.
The forefoot tapers more than some rivals; runners with a wide forefoot often look for the wide version.
Balanced, medium-soft cushioning and a medium-volume upper with a comfortable heel hold.
HOKA's most cushioned road shoe: a very soft, high-stack ride with a broad, stable base.
Plush, high-volume upper and a thick heel collar for a secure heel; the toe box is moderate to roomy.
Available in wide and extra-wide versions, among the broader options for very wide feet.
A light, responsive trainer for tempo runs and faster days, with a firmer, snappier feel than the Clifton.
A thin, low-volume upper with a snug, performance fit; the toe box is not especially roomy.
Minimal heel padding; heel hold depends on lacing more than in plusher HOKA models.
A stability shoe that uses a firmer frame along the medial side instead of a traditional post, so it feels close to neutral.
Medium-volume upper with a structured heel; balanced, medium-firm cushioning.
The midfoot feels supportive and the forefoot is moderate in width.
A versatile neutral daily trainer with balanced, medium cushioning and a moderate drop.
Medium-volume upper with a comfortable, moderately roomy toe box and a secure heel.
A conventional fit that suits many foot shapes; firmer than max-cushion shoes.
A stability daily trainer with guidance from a wider base and sidewalls rather than a hard post.
Medium-volume upper and a secure heel counter; balanced, medium-firm cushioning.
Toe box is moderate; a good fit for medium-width feet that want a stable feel.
A plated tempo trainer (nylon plate) with a bouncy, propulsive ride for workouts and race-pace runs.
A light, low-volume upper with a snug midfoot; the toe box is moderate.
Heel hold is secure for a fast shoe; less padding than daily trainers.
Saucony's max-cushion neutral trainer with a soft, springy high-stack ride for long and easy runs.
A plush, medium-to-high-volume upper with a padded heel collar for a secure heel.
The forefoot is moderately roomy.
A soft, max-cushion neutral trainer for easy and long runs.
A roomy toe box with room for toe splay, with a medium-volume upper.
Made in wide and extra-wide versions, a popular choice for wide forefeet.
A durable, conventional daily trainer with balanced, medium-firm cushioning.
A medium-volume upper with a secure, padded heel; the toe box is moderate.
Offered in wide and extra-wide versions, suiting wide feet that want a traditional fit.
A versatile daily trainer with a responsive, medium-firm ride that handles easy runs and some faster work.
The forefoot is on the narrower side; runners with a wide forefoot often find the toe box tight.
Secure heel hold with a padded collar; medium-volume upper.
Nike's max-cushion daily trainer with a soft, high-stack ride for easy and long runs.
A plush, padded upper with a medium-to-high-volume feel and a secure heel.
The toe box is moderate; a fuller fit than the Pegasus.
A very soft, bouncy max-cushion shoe for recovery and easy runs, with a wide base.
A medium-volume knit upper; the forefoot is moderate, and heel lock can feel less secure than in more structured shoes.
The soft foam can feel less stable on corners than firmer shoes.
Zero-drop: the heel and forefoot sit at the same height, which feels very different from traditional shoes and takes time to adapt to.
Altra's foot-shaped toe box is very roomy and lets toes spread, a strong option for wide forefeet.
Balanced, medium cushioning; the heel is narrower than the forefoot, which helps heel hold for a wide forefoot with a narrow heel.
